A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ResCP study. The main text, equations, proofs, nine tables, ten figures, and appendices are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original forecasting experiments on four real-world datasets, a synthetic autoregressive experiment, ablations, and sensitivity analyses in Section 4 and Appendices D–F.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and analyses, including revised ACEA results in Tables 1, 5, and 6.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same reservoir dynamics, similarity-based residual weighting, Monte Carlo quantiles, interval-width optimization, temporal decay, sliding window, and ResCQR readout with pinball loss.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Solar, Beijing, Exchange, ACEA, and the same synthetic AR(1) process with changing coefficients. Exogenous-input scenarios and forecasting tasks are unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain SCP, NexCP, SPCI, HopCPT, CP-QRNN, and ResCQR. The synthetic comparison in Table 7 also retains the same ablated variants, NexCP, and SCP.

E3.justification: The stated data splits, point predictors, metrics, training budgets, validation procedures, sampling settings, and hyperparameter selections remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices B–D. No reported protocol revision accompanies the changed ACEA scores.

E4.justification: The temporal-decay and window ablations, synthetic shift experiment, exogenous-variable comparisons, calibration curves, adaptive-interval examples, and hyperparameter sensitivity analyses are retained with the same evidence in Tables 3 and 7–9 and Figures 2–10.

E5.justification: Both already display ± quantities and shaded uncertainty bands. v3 adds no run counts, seeds, explanations of those quantities, or statistical tests; changes to individual ± values are result revisions.

E6.justification: Numerical revisions are confined to HopCPT, CP-QRNN, and ResCQR on ACEA in Tables 1, 5, and 6. For example, Table 1's Transformer CP-QRNN ΔCov changes from -21.92±9.88 to -13.35±9.85, while Table 5's ARIMA ResCQR Winkler score changes from 81.25±14.59 to 67.04±12.20. ResCP's scores and leading ACEA Winkler ranking remain unchanged, limiting the effect on the main findings.

T1.justification: Assumptions 3.1–3.5, the effective-sample-size definition, Theorem 3.6, Corollary 3.7, and Appendix A's proofs are mathematically unchanged. The quantile-consistency sentence receives only a grammatical refinement.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free reservoir conformal prediction, scalability, asymptotic conditional coverage, and extensions for distribution shifts and exogenous variables.

C2.justification: Both retain the same qualifications about conditioning on reservoir states versus full histories, finite-sample bias, distribution shifts, covariate sensitivity, and hyperparameter tradeoffs. The added generic ethics statement introduces no substantive scientific limitation or interpretation.

D1.justification: The code-release promise moves from Appendix G to Appendix J and drops 'upon publication,' leaving release timing unspecified. Neither PDF supplies a link to the study's code; implementation descriptions, software, hardware, and hyperparameters are otherwise unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to earlier conformal-prediction and reservoir-computing research are retained. Expanded author names, reordered bibliography entries, and citation formatting do not introduce new literature.

P1.justification: v3 corrects isolated wording, updates author-contribution information and acknowledgments, and adds short appendices on LLM use, ethics, and reproducibility. The scientific section sequence and nearly all explanatory prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The conference template substantially changes typography, text-block width, display sizes, and float placement throughout. Figures 4–5 now share a page, as do Figures 7–8 and 9–10, replacing separate-page arrangements. All nine tables and ten figures are retained; the figure graphics themselves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The revised ACEA values leave ResCP's results and the principal conclusions intact, while the methods, proofs, and supplementary evidence remain unchanged. Small wording fixes and a more compact layout offer limited presentation benefits, with smaller displays and less specific code-release timing as tradeoffs. Together, these changes produce no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
